page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.4xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented virtual machine configuration built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz, providing 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory is configured at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per thread. Bundled local storage is absent, requiring external block volumes for operational data retention. Network connectivity provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps, and no hardware GPU accelerators are included.

Processor capabilities include vector extensions such as AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration and FMA. Benchmark evaluations position the instance predominantly in the mid-tier range for compute workloads, producing a stress-ng single-core score of 1578.98, a multi-core score of 16657.34, a Geekbench single-core score of 1253.0, and a multi-core score of 7455.0. Static web serving throughput reaches 9.51 GB/sec, while in-memory operations register 15.83 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware constraints appear in memory subsystem throughput, where the PassMark memory benchmark reflects lower-quartile performance at 1797.16, and medium model LLM prompt evaluation yields 22.42 tokens per second.

With its 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio and reliance on external storage arrays, the ecs.c4.4xlarge represents a resource-balanced compute environment for workloads not gated by extreme memory footprints. Suitable applications include software build pipelines, as demonstrated by a Clang compilation score of 14249.0, continuous integration runners, high-throughput static web serving, and distributed batch processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.4xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates over a KVM hypervisor with 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, omitting bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. Benchmark performance remains largely in the mid-tier range, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 17360.29, Geekbench multi-core rating of 7455.0, and static web serving throughput of 9.51 GB/sec. Conversely, memory subsystem benchmarking indicates lower relative throughput with a PassMark memory score in the bottom quartile. The ecs.c4.4xlarge is well tailored for CPU-intensive tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving, and caching layers that utilize external storage.
